messages.author: d1915bd7eb8a8373
messages.subject: R Aborting During Sampling
parts:
Hi all,

A few weeks ago I tried Nimble HMC using the beta version of Nimble, and then recently decided to switch back and I reinstalled the current version of Nimble. However, now whenever I go to run sampling on any compiled model, R encounters a fatal error and aborts. R aborts even when running previous versions of models that worked fine a few weeks ago, and on an example model from the Nimble user manual that should have been able to run. I've tried reinstalling R, Rstudio, and Rtools to make sure that everything is up to date, and that failed to solve the issue. Has anyone encountered an issue like this before?

Thanks,
Jen

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: R Aborting During Sampling
parts:
Well, that sounds disconcerting. A few things to check:

1) Let's make sure you have the non-AD-enabled nimble installed. This should return `NULL`:

> nimbleOptions('enableDerivs')

2) What's the exact error message you get when you run the example from the manual (and which example are you running)?

3) Also, to see if your Rtools is working, please try to run a basic Rcpp operation (I'm assuming here that you have Rcpp installed, but you can install it if not):

> Rcpp::cppFunction(
          'int fibonacci(const int x) {
              if (x == 0) return(0);
              if (x == 1) return(1);
              return (fibonacci(x - 1)) + fibonacci(x - 2);
          }')
> fibonacci(7)

-chris

messages.subject: Re: R Aborting During Sampling
parts:
Hi Chris,

Thank you for your response!

1)  nimbleOptions('enableDerivs') does return NULL, so all good there.

2) The error message R gives me whenever I run any mcmc is the pop-up "R Session Aborted. R encountered a fatal error. The session was terminated" and it gives me the option to start a new session. The example from the manual I tried was the brief example from the lightning introduction:

pumpCode <- nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:N){
    theta[i] ~ dgamma(alpha,beta)
    lambda[i] <- theta[i]*t[i]
    x[i] ~ dpois(lambda[i])
  }
  alpha ~ dexp(1.0)
  beta ~ dgamma(0.1,1.0)
})

pumpConsts <- list(N = 10,
                   t = c(94.3, 15.7, 62.9, 126, 5.24,
                         31.4, 1.05, 1.05, 2.1, 10.5))

pumpData <- list(x = c(5, 1, 5, 14, 3, 19, 1, 1, 4, 22))

pumpInits <- list(alpha = 1, beta = 1,
                  theta = rep(0.1, pumpConsts$N))

pump <- nimbleModel(code = pumpCode, name = "pump", constants = pumpConsts,
                    data = pumpData, inits = pumpInits)

pumpConf <- configureMCMC(pump, print = TRUE)

pumpMCMC <- buildMCMC(pumpConf)

Cpump <- compileNimble(pump)

CpumpMCMC <- compileNimble(pumpMCMC, project = pump)

CpumpMCMC$run(niter = 10, nburnin = 1, thin = 0)

3) The Rcpp operation worked fine, so it appears Rtools is working.

Thanks,
Jen

messages.subject: Re: R Aborting During Sampling
parts:
Hmm, the mystery persists. 

Throwing some thing up against the wall...

1) Any chance you have a .Rda or .RData file in the directory from which you are starting R (or RStudio) that might load objects into your R global environment that might somehow be causing a problem? (I'm trying to think of what would cause some sort of persistent state that would be affecting your sessions even after all the re-installation you did.)

2) If you start a plain R session (not RStudio) do you have the same problem? 

3) I'm wondering if the issue is with any operations involving code compiled by nimble or just the MCMC.

Can you do anything with the compiled model, such as:

> Cpump$calculate()

4) You could try installing nimble again in a different location on your file system and see if the same issue occurs:

install.packages(pkgs, lib = "/path/to/somewhere/in/your/home/directory")
library(nimble, lib.loc = "/path/to/somewhere/in/your/home/directory")

-chris
